Retrieve the service relationships for a specific monitor.

Each relationship records how the monitor relates to another service:
`depends_on` (directed), `shares_infrastructure_with`, or `same_provider`
(both symmetric). Every relationship includes the `service` it points to,
the `monitor` it belongs to, and `source` describing how it was
discovered.

Retrieve active components for a specific monitor with status information.

**Behavior:**
- **StatusPageService monitors with no component filters:** Returns all components from the service (monitoring all components)
- **StatusPageService monitors with component filters:** Returns only the filtered/subscribed components
- **Non-StatusPageService monitors (WebsiteMonitor, PingMonitor, etc.):** Returns empty array

Components include current status.

summary: Remove a subscriber from the board's status page by providing either id or email in the request body
Get all confirmed email subscribers for a board's status page

Creates a status page subscription for the specified board. Provide the subscriber's `email`; use `monitor_ids` to target specific monitors or omit it to subscribe to all monitors. A confirmation email is sent unless `skip_confirmation` is true, and a 201 response returns the created subscriber.

Create a new service monitor for the specified board. Service monitors
        allow you to subscribe to status page services and track their status on your board.

Create a new website monitor for the specified board. Website monitors
        allow you to monitor the uptime and performance of websites and APIs. You can
        configure various monitoring options including check intervals, content monitoring,
        HTTP methods, and notification preferences.

Create a new custom monitor for the specified board. Custom monitors
        allow you to add manually managed services to your status page. You can update
        their status manually as needed.
Get all monitor groups for a board. Monitor groups allow you to organize monitors into logical categories for better organization and display on status pages.

Creates a monitor group to organize monitors on a board. Supply a `name` and, optionally, a `position` to control the group's display order, with lower numbers appearing first. The response includes the created group and its identifier.
List the outage reports submitted through the board's status page, newest first. To poll for new reports, pass `since` with the time of your previous request.

Creates an outage report for a monitor on a board. Include `monitor_id` in `outage_report`, and optionally provide affected `component_ids`, a reporter `email`, and a `comment` of up to 300 characters. A 201 response returns the created report and triggers side effects.

Create a new ping monitor for the specified board. Ping monitors
        allow you to monitor the uptime and connectivity of hosts by sending ICMP ping
        requests. You can configure various monitoring options including check intervals,
        timeout settings, and notification preferences.
Retrieve all active components for a specific service. Components represent individual parts or subsystems of a service that are monitored separately (like API, Dashboard, Database, etc.).
Lists incidents for a specific board, including their current phases and severity levels. Filter by `phase` or `severity`, and use `page` and `per_page` to paginate the results.

summary: Returns a list of historical events affecting monitors on a board over a date range.
Deletes a service monitor from a board. Use `board_id` and `id` to identify the board and the service monitor to remove; the response confirms whether deletion succeeded.
Update a service monitor. You can update the name, description, and monitor group assignment.
Deletes a website monitor from a board. Use the `board_id` and `id` path parameters to identify the board and monitor to remove. A successful response includes a boolean `success` value.

Update an existing website monitor. You can modify any of the
        monitoring configuration options including check intervals, content monitoring,
        HTTP methods, and notification preferences.
Deletes a custom monitor from a board. Use `board_id` and `id` to identify the board and the custom monitor to remove. A successful response confirms the deletion.

Updates an existing custom monitor on a board. Supply any combination of `name`, `description`, `metadata`, and `monitor_group_id` to change those properties. Set `monitor_group_id` to null to remove the monitor from its group.
Delete a monitor group. Any monitors assigned to this group will become ungrouped.
Retrieves the details of a specific monitor group on a board. Use the board and monitor group identifiers to select the group.
Updates an existing monitor group's name or display position on a board. Supply the fields you want to change in `monitor_group`; lower `position` values place the group earlier in the display order.
Deletes a ping monitor from a board. Use `board_id` and `id` to identify the board and the ping monitor to remove.

Update an existing ping monitor. You can modify any of the

Retrieve all available monitoring regions that StatusGator
      uses to check website or ping monitors. Monitoring regions are geographic
      locations with fixed IP addresses from which StatusGator monitors your
      services. Use this API to retrieve the IP addresses, allowing you to
      whitelist them in your firewall.

Access to this API endpoint is restricted to customers with
      Firehose. integration access. Retrieve all available services that
      StatusGator monitors. Services represent external platforms and tools
      (like GitHub, AWS, Slack, etc.) that StatusGator tracks for status
      updates. StatusGator checks these services every 5 minutes and provides
      real-time status information.

summary:
Retrieve all boards belonging to your organization. Boards
        are like projects that display the status of selected services you depend
        on. Each board allows you to organize and monitor specific groups of
        services relevant to your operations. Results are paginated for efficient
        data retrieval.

Creates a new board in your organization. Pass `user_ids` to assign organization users; without them, the board has no user assignments and does not appear in any user's web sidebar, though it remains accessible through the API. A 201 response returns the created board and its public token.

Retrieve all users belonging to your organization. Users are
      members of your organization who can access StatusGator dashboards,
      configure monitoring settings, and receive notifications. Users can have
      either the role of org_admin or editor.

Authentication check and whoami. Returns a success message plus the organization
and token the supplied bearer token belongs to, so an integration can confirm
a token is valid and show which account it is connected to.

Delete a board. The board is soft-deleted (discarded). You
        cannot delete your only remaining board.
Retrieves details for a specific board. Use the board's public ID in `id` to identify which board to retrieve.
Updates a board's name, its assigned organization users, or both. Supply the board fields you want to change in `board`; passing an empty `user_ids` array removes all user assignments.
